title: SymFT: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuit Simulation via Symbolic Clifford--Pauli Frames and Stabilizer Coordinates
conversion_notes: The benchmark describes distillation.stim as an extended Stim-like near-Clifford circuit containing non-Clifford operations; inspect the file for its exact gates and rotation conventions. SymFT and Clifft rotation arguments are in half-turns.
notes: The benchmark README identifies distillation.stim as an 85-qubit [[17,1,5]] magic-state distillation workload, usable with Tsim/Clifft/SymFT. The paper is about simulation, not the original protocol. README groups this file with circuits containing T, T_DAG, R_X or R_Z without specifying which of these occur in this specific file; classify as native non-Clifford rather than asserting a specific gate. Source circuit direct page could not be fetched by web tool.

title: Clifft: Fast Exact Simulation of Near-Clifford Quantum Circuits
conversion_notes: Published cultivation_d3.stim and cultivation_d5.stim are native near-Clifford circuit fixtures. SymFT benchmark identifies exact copies msc_d3_inject_cultivate_p1e-3.stim and msc_d5_inject_cultivate_p1e-3.stim; no S-to-T substitution is needed.
notes: Simulation paper; benchmark fixtures derived from Gidney et al. Use d=3 Steane/color code and d=5 growth. SymFT benchmark supplies immutable upstream Clifft commit db7dc9f13a2c2854690e92390c779048a1ac1400 and notes its d=7 workload is unverified; do not use d=7 for logical error claims.

title: Magic state cultivation: growing T states as cheap as CNOT gates
conversion_notes: Cultivation uses a Clifford S/S_DAG proxy for the corresponding T/T_DAG injection and logical-HXY verification rotations; substitute only protocol-designated proxy gates, not arbitrary S gates. Native converted d=3 and d=5 fixtures exist in Clifft and SymFT benchmarks.
notes: Author data identified by Stim circuit data catalog; Zenodo DOI could not be opened by web tool. SymFT README identifies original generator commit 871e68ff6df2f75190b1bfd6351459d1b5a037e3, and Clifft-derived circuits, with d=3 and d=5 specialized growth and verification. Overlaps other cultivation searches.

title: Quantum Circuit Discovery for Fault-Tolerant Logical State Preparation with Reinforcement Learning
authors: Zen, Olle, Colmenarez, Puviani, Müller, Marquardt
conversion_notes: Only a stabilizer-state encoder and verification building block is demonstrated: making a magic state requires a separately designed non-Clifford preparation and compatible verification, not a simple gate substitution.
notes: Author repository explicitly supplies Stim circuits and generators, including seven-qubit Steane |0> and flag-based verification. It does not demonstrate non-stabilizer preparation; a possible source of components only and outside strict selection criteria.

title: Flag at origin: a modular fault-tolerant preparation for CSS codes
conversion_notes: The [[17,1,5]] output is a |0> stabilizer preparation with flags, not a magic-state proxy. One must construct and validate an appropriate non-Clifford preparation and verification protocol; do not replace a random Clifford gate.
notes: QECirc provides a downloadable Stim rendering for a 17-qubit color-code FT |0> circuit, traced to paper source Notebook_1/SeventeenColorCode.json; also reusable flag gadgets. Third-party conversion of author circuits, not an author-released magic circuit. Included as a limited building-block lead.

title: Automated Synthesis of Fault-Tolerant State Preparation Circuits for Quantum Error Correction Codes
conversion_notes: Synthesizes verified CSS stabilizer preparation; extension to a non-Clifford magic-state protocol requires additional state injection and proper verification, not a simple replacement of a gate.
notes: Stim project catalog lists paper Stim circuits; paper points to author MQT QECC repository and describes distance-3 and distance-5 preparation and verification. No released magic-state circuit established; retained as a possible building-block source only.
